name: IronClaw
vibe_summary: A Rust-based Agent OS from NEAR AI that positions itself as a privacy-first, security-hardened personal AI assistant with encrypted local storage and no telemetry. Its extremely rigorous commit culture (contract tests, architecture gates, fail-closed design) signals a production-grade, security-obsessed engineering ethos.
best_for: Privacy-conscious users wanting a local-first assistant
Teams needing auditable, fail-closed agent security
Rust developers extending a typed agent platform
avoid_if: You want the largest possible skill/plugin ecosystem
You need a mature, battle-tested community at OpenClaw scale
You rely on niche chat channels not yet supported
openclaw_advantages: Encrypted local credential store with secrets kept out of LLM context
Fail-closed pairing/binding model with contract-tested security gates
Rust performance and memory safety versus OpenClaw's runtime
No telemetry and explicit anti-data-harvesting design
Rigorous architecture gates and contract tests reduce regression risk
openclaw_disadvantages: Far smaller community and mindshare (12.6k vs 300k+ stars)
Fewer supported chat channels and integrations
Heavier conceptual complexity (contracts, gates) for casual users
Younger project with less third-party documentation and tutorials
confidence_summary: Strong evidence from README, license, release metadata, and highly detailed recent commits supports the security and privacy assessments. Community sentiment is positive but drawn mostly from the project's own subreddit, so independent validation is thinner.

overview_markdown:
IronClaw is an Agent OS written in Rust by NEAR AI, built around the principle that your AI assistant should work for you, not against you. All data is stored locally and encrypted, credentials live in an encrypted store kept out of the LLM's context, and the project explicitly rejects telemetry and data harvesting. It ships with a guided onboarding flow (`ironclaw onboard`), a background service, and a WebUI, with installers for macOS, Linux, and Windows/WSL.

Architecturally, IronClaw is unusually rigorous for an agent project: recent commits show contract-tier and e2e-tier tests, fail-closed pairing and device-link flows, architecture gates that pin crate size ceilings, and careful privacy work such as hashing thread IDs before they leave the process as OpenAI prompt-cache keys. It supports multiple LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI Responses and chat-completions paths, GitHub Copilot, NEAR AI), subagent orchestration with approval/auth gates surfaced to a human owner's inbox, and channel integrations like Telegram and Slack.

Compared to OpenClaw, IronClaw trades ecosystem size for security posture: it has a fraction of OpenClaw's stars, skills, and channel breadth, but offers a hardened, auditable Rust core with encrypted local state and a privacy-first philosophy. It is best suited to users and teams who prioritize verifiable security and data sovereignty over the largest possible plugin catalog.
